label: Any two actual beings whose esse is their essence share one nature
paraphrase: OPEN analyst premise, attribution deferred: any two beings in act as to being, each of whose represented esse equals its represented essence, share one nature (SharesNature), so that their being two would be a multiplication of that nature. SharesNature is not defined as equality of essence values, a common predicate, or numerical identity of the bearers. The strongest positive rationale reads the identity as addition-excluding subsistent esse: no further quidditative content determines different whole kinds. That act/determination account can warrant direct primitive acceptance; represented equality alone does not prove its application. De ente c.3 [69874] treats esse tantum as one nature without separately arguing the whole-nature exclusion. A distinct-whole-nature reply posits intrinsically differentiated unreceived acts; it owes a positive account of that application. Bare numerical thisness accepting common nature instead challenges the three-mode multiplication inventory. TwoSourcesControl is an omission result, not evidence that an actual or metaphysically possible identity bearer violates this premise. Current positive warrant, rival comparison, q11 distinctions, retained dependencies and reopening conditions: docs/notes/de-ente-esse-source-1628.md, Current source-selection judgment (2026-11-17).
